| Scene description | • S07-A is near Optics Valley Square Metro Station, photographed on November 11, 2026, at 11:37 in cloudy weather. Green roadside and barrier-side bins are worn, stained, and poorly labeled.<br>• S07-A-01: a non-overflowing green food-waste bin stands near electric bicycles.<br>• S07-A-02: waste in a blue bicycle basket is recognized as overflowing; a damaged yellow crate, rubble, and minor litter occur beside planting.<br>• S07-A-04: three old green bins stand at yellow barriers. Two are recognized as overflowing with bags and foam food containers; some lids are closed, while another is open without obvious spillage. Unattached images had no detected targets and are not described. |
| Regulatory basis | • Containers should be clean, intact, clearly labeled, and appropriately located without impairing pedestrians or appearance. Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 15.<br>• Overflow and accumulation require timely collection against secondary pollution. Measures for the Management of Municipal Solid Waste, Article 22.<br>• Indiscriminate dumping or stockpiling at undesignated locations or in non-sorting containers is prohibited. Measures for the Management of Municipal Solid Waste, Article 25.<br>• Food waste, recyclables, and other waste require separate disposal with clear labels. Implementation Plan for the Municipal Solid Waste Classification System (State Council General Office Document〔2017〕26), Article 3.<br>• Subdistrict or property managers must inspect collection points and respond promptly. Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 17.<br>• Improper sorting or delayed collection may incur warnings, fines, or suspension in serious cases where correction is refused or pollution or public-order impacts occur. Measures for the Management of Municipal Solid Waste, Article 39. |
| Severity | **Moderate.** Three overflows and one accumulation, old and poorly labeled bins, and ground litter impair appearance and public order near a busy station and risk spread, without severe pollution or blockage. |
| Impact assessment | Visible impacts: spillage and ground litter impair passage and appearance; unclear labels may misguide sorting. Possible short-term impacts: delays may cause vectors, odors, and disease risks, with complaints or media attention in a busy station area. |
| Potential causes | - **Possible cause 1:** delayed collection; two of three old bins at S07-A-04 overflow, some lids closed, suggesting prolonged retention. Check frequency records.<br>- **Possible cause 2:** weak sorting awareness; waste in the S07-A-02 bicycle basket indicates undesignated disposal. Check education or supervision.<br>- **Possible cause 3:** inadequate capacity or layout at constrained barriers; compare generation and provision where two of three bins overflow. |
| Long-term effects | If persistent or recurrent, routine accumulation may breed vectors and intensify pollution; unclear labels or damaged bins may weaken sorting and participation; dissatisfaction in public station areas may damage the city's civic image. |
| Recommendations | - **Immediate actions:** remove overflow and accumulation at S07-A-02 and S07-A-04, sweep litter, clean or replace damaged and heavily stained bins, and add conspicuous guidance.<br>- **Long-term measures:** match numbers and capacity to demand; increase inspections and log collections; educate users; assess and supervise station or subdistrict managers. |
| Priority | **High.** Overflow and accumulation in a busy station area affect public surroundings and pose sanitation and complaint risks. Prioritized action should prevent wider harm. |
